summary: Lineup is right as it stands and there is no claim worth making — Thomas already landed. Three opponent starters are game-time calls; only one has a handcuff worth a free claim.

items.headline: Malik Nabers — game-time decision
items.evidence: Full practice Friday and off the practice report, but the Giants left him questionable and both he and Harbaugh declined to confirm. Beat consensus is that he plays; he has said the call is his and he will not risk the knee. Sunday night game, so you will know last.
items.body: Footballers' WR1. If he sits, Malachi Fields is the direct beneficiary at 8.9% rostered and free. Chem priority resets weekly so the claim costs nothing — but it is a lottery ticket on a player who is probably playing, and you would be dropping someone to hold it.

items.headline: Rome Odunze — plays, calf
items.evidence: Limited a third straight day and officially questionable, but he told reporters he plans to play. A calf that practices three days is a snap-count story, not an availability one.
items.body: Los Gigantes' WR1. No handcuff available — Burden is rostered by Bok-aneers and Loveland by Nicky Jam. Nothing to claim here; this is a note, not a move.

items.headline: Jeremiyah Love — plays, but he is the RB2
items.evidence: High ankle sprain from mid-August, limited Thursday, and Garafolo's source put Week 1 at 50-50. LaFleur now says he feels good about him being in the lineup. The Cardinals' first regular-season depth chart lists Allgeier RB1 and Love RB2.
items.body: Aye-Aye drafted him at ADP 25 as a bell cow and is starting him. He is behind your own Tyler Allgeier on the official chart. That is worth knowing before you offer for him in two weeks, and worth knowing about Allgeier now.

items.headline: Allgeier's 6.9 is stale — he is Arizona's listed RB1
items.evidence: Cardinals' Week 1 depth chart has Allgeier first and Love second. ESPN still projects him as a backup because Love was drafted third overall.
items.body: Still sits this week — Tuten at 10.9 and Warren at 11.3 are both ahead of him even discounted. But do not drop him for a marginal TE upgrade: a two-man committee where he is the listed starter is worth more than 6.9 implies.

items.headline: McLaurin holds the flex over Warren
items.evidence: Off the injury report entirely, full practices Thursday and Friday, Washington cleared its whole squad for Philadelphia. Warren is in a committee where Dowdle is expected to take early downs, and Warren's edge is receiving — worth half in this league.
items.body: ESPN has Warren 11.3 to McLaurin 10.1. This is the one place this week where the projection and the reporting disagree, and the reporting wins.

items.headline: Jaguars D/ST is the consensus number-one defense this week
items.evidence: Cleveland carries the lowest implied team total on the slate behind the worst-graded offensive line in the league, and Jacksonville is a 7.5-point home favourite.
items.body: Already started. The related exposure is worth naming: Tuten, Thomas and the defence are all Jacksonville, so one blowout moves three of your slots together.

items.headline: Tuten is a co-starter, not a lead back
items.evidence: Jacksonville lists Tuten and Chris Rodriguez as co-starters and the beat expects a near-even split. The draft-board read that only an injured Rodriguez sat behind him was wrong.
items.body: He still starts at RB2 because nothing better exists. LeQuint Allen's hip likely keeps him out, which pushes pass-down work to Tuten — worth less here at half PPR than it would be in IPADE. Treat 10.9 as the ceiling.
